title: Stateless tp pickup front door for signed shelf Design Contracts
summary: Add one bounded CLI adapter that verifies repository-resident approved Design authority at an exact clean SHA, derives a one-element in-memory micro-plan, enters the incumbent BUILD-C direct-assignment/checkpoint/merge boundaries one AC at a time, and persists the only resumable handoff as a Git-tracked content-addressed receipt chain.

current_state.summary: At exact baseline 726acd108d3ca431e680183de129918842202eda, tp.py has no pickup command. build_c.py already owns direct graph-disjoint assignment and exact green-checkpoint integration; checkpoint.py owns exact-revision checkpoint specs and engine-minted receipts; design_contract.py owns Design evidence fingerprints/current approval validation; repository.py owns registered worktree merge receipts; storage.py exposes the private state surfaces pickup must not create. The supplied graph baseline is e0d54a84434269c488941a265f865803c90c7e8adaa0796159ea60a3257adc8b with 50 modules and 165 edges. No stateless shelf front door or repository pickup receipt chain exists.

constraints: Only tp pickup for one selected Design Contract element is in scope; no Phase 0, E0, R-0011, or other R-0013 content.
The hook security layer and legacy loop path remain byte- and behavior-unchanged.
Pickup creates no run, track, wave, claim, lease, stage, per-task-lens, or equivalent private coordination record.
Existing approved-Design, BUILD-C direct-assignment, checkpoint, and repository merge contracts are consumption boundaries, not redesign authority.
Manual delivery advances one acceptance criterion at a time; behavior and its focused test share the implementation commit.
Version 2.17.20 metadata follows functional green; push, tag, publish, and origin/main mutation require later human authority.

quality_targets.measurement: Monotonic timestamps at public CLI entry and pickup.checkpoint.started in a fresh checkout with an empty private Taskplane home and no warmed process.
Instrument storage mutation entry points and compare the isolated TASKPLANE_HOME tree before and after pickup and second-checkout resume.

quality_targets.threshold: exactly one contiguous successor per completed criterion; 0 forks, gaps, overwrites, or digest mismatches
quality_targets.measurement: Recompute canonical receipt/path/predecessor digests while scanning the source-SHA/Design-fingerprint/element directory.
python -m pytest taskplane/tests -q on the final clean SHA compared with the exact baseline result.

alternatives.name: Thin stateless adapter over BUILD-C
alternatives.description: Add pickup.py and minimum explicit-input façades while retaining the incumbent Design approval, direct assignment, checkpoint, and repository merge owners.

gains: Satisfies zero orchestration state and Git-only resume
Reuses the live checkpoint and green-integration validation
Keeps hook security and the legacy loop unchanged
costs: BUILD-C needs a small explicit-input façade beside its loop-state wrapper
Pickup must validate append-only receipt lineage and collision behavior
tradeoffs.revisit_when: More than one selected element must be scheduled concurrently, or an incumbent boundary cannot accept explicit verified inputs without a separately approved semantic redesign.

alternatives.name: Ephemeral loop then cleanup
alternatives.description: Create a normal loop and synthetic one-task Plan, execute through it, then delete the private state.

gains: Requires little new BUILD-C adapter code
costs: Creates forbidden run and equivalent coordination state
Cleanup destroys or strands interruption evidence
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only under a replacement Product requirement that explicitly permits private orchestration state.

alternatives.name: Independent pickup executor and merger
alternatives.description: Implement assignment, command execution, checkpoint receipts, worktree ownership, and merge directly in pickup.py.

gains: No adapter changes in existing owners
costs: Duplicates the checkpoint and merge trust boundaries
Violates the required pickup-to-BUILD-C edge and explicit out-of-scope rules
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The incumbent BUILD-C/checkpoint/repository contracts are formally retired by a separately approved migration.

alternatives.name: Status quo
alternatives.description: Leave signed shelf Design Contracts executable only through private loop state.

costs: Does not satisfy AC1 through AC4
Cannot provide the intended first production pickup use

decision: Select the thin stateless BUILD-C adapter because it is the only option that simultaneously preserves existing approval/checkpoint/merge ownership, creates zero private orchestration handoff state, proves a live pickup-to-BUILD-C edge, and makes another checkout resumable from Git-tracked authority and receipts. If an incumbent boundary requires semantic redesign or a new signer, stop for human scope rather than widening this adapter.

contracts.description: One repository-local command verifies exact shelf authority, derives one in-memory micro-plan, and enters existing BUILD-C boundaries without orchestration state.
Existing signed approved Design evidence, approval, engine receipt, authorized source SHA, and recomputed Design fingerprint validation.
Existing graph-disjoint exact-scope assignment semantics exposed through an explicit-input one-element façade.
Existing one-AC exact-revision checkpoint specification, governed-command observation, and engine-green receipt authority.
Existing repository owner integrates only the exact BUILD-C-authorized green revision and returns its merge receipt.
Append-only Git-tracked receipt lineage keyed by authorized source SHA and Design evidence fingerprint, sufficient for private-store-free resume.

proposed_edges.reason: The public pickup parser delegates once to the bounded pickup coordinator.
Pickup owns exact preflight, one-element micro-planning, ordered AC advancement, and named refusal boundaries.
The incumbent Design owner recomputes evidence identity and verifies existing signed approval and engine receipt authority.
Pickup cannot plan or execute until repository authority, approval, engine receipt, source SHA, and Design fingerprint agree.
BUILD-C remains the owner of graph-disjoint direct assignment and explicit-scope validation.
The one-element micro-plan enters the incumbent direct-assignment boundary without creating loop state.
The incumbent checkpoint owner validates exact HEAD/scope/proof/runtime evidence and mints engine-green receipts.
Pickup advances exactly one current AC only through the existing checkpoint contract.
RepositoryManager remains the sole worktree identity and ordinary Git merge owner.
Pickup records a merge only after BUILD-C authorizes the exact green assigned revision.
Pickup persists the only resumable handoff as a content-addressed Git-tracked receipt chain.
This is the mandatory live pickup-to-BUILD-C seam; severing it must fail AC3.
The pickup BUILD-C façade invokes the incumbent exact-revision checkpoint owner.
BUILD-C green authorization delegates exact-revision integration to the incumbent repository owner.
Focused acceptance, cold-start, mutation, collision, interruption, and second-checkout proofs exercise the public pickup coordinator.
Negative instrumentation proves pickup creates no private orchestration record and resume reads no private handoff.

depth_policy.rationale: Inspect the local adapter and incumbent owners to depth 3, then stop after one hop at each named Design, BUILD-C, checkpoint, repository, exports, or requirement boundary.

dor.check: Exact baseline identity is captured before Design mutation.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC1 — a shelf contract runs end-to-end via pickup with zero run/track state (trace evidence). Verify with a signed shelf fixture and trace assertions covering pickup through the existing BUILD-C checkpoint and green integration while proving zero run, track, claim, lease, wave, or equivalent state.
acceptance_map.validation: Run taskplane/tests/test_pickup.py::test_signed_shelf_pickup_reaches_checkpoint_and_green_merge_without_orchestration_state through the public CLI seam; assert ordered pickup→BUILD-C→checkpoint→repository trace and exactly zero private orchestration mutations/home records.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC2 — cold start on a fresh checkout at the same SHA to first executing checkpoint in <2 minutes. Verify with a wall-clock integration test from a fresh checkout, empty private Taskplane home, exact authorized SHA, and no warmed or inherited runtime state.
acceptance_map.validation: Run taskplane/tests/test_pickup.py::test_fresh_checkout_reaches_first_executing_checkpoint_under_120_seconds with a new checkout, empty TASKPLANE_HOME, no warm process, exact authority SHA, and monotonic CLI-entry/checkpoint-start timestamps requiring elapsed < 120.0 seconds.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC3 — severed-edge tests: cutting the pickup→build_c entry fails; legacy loop path untouched and its suite still green. Verify with a severed pickup-to-BUILD-C seam and the unchanged legacy-loop regression selectors.
acceptance_map.validation: Run taskplane/tests/test_pickup.py::test_severed_pickup_to_build_c_edge_fails and require the end-to-end fixture to fail when the call is cut; also run python -m pytest taskplane/tests/test_loop.py taskplane/tests/test_r0007_governed_commands.py -q against byte-unchanged loop/hook sources.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC4 — a second checkout resumes from repo-resident receipts with no private-store handoff. Verify after at least one manual criterion using only Git-tracked Design authority and exports receipts at the same SHA and Design fingerprint.
acceptance_map.validation: Run taskplane/tests/test_pickup.py::test_second_checkout_resumes_from_git_receipts_without_private_home: complete one AC, commit its export, remove access to the first home, clone/checkout the recorded lineage, and resume using only tracked authority/receipt bytes for the same authorized-source-SHA/Design-fingerprint identity.

acceptance_map.criterion: AC5 — full suite on the final SHA: no new failures. Verify with python -m pytest taskplane/tests -q on the final clean commit against the exact baseline; any new failure blocks release review.
acceptance_map.validation: On the final clean commit run python -m pytest taskplane/tests -q, record exact SHA/argv/result counts, and compare with the exact baseline; any new failure blocks release review.

risks.risk: A digest lookalike or caller boolean is accepted as Design approval or engine authority.
risks.mitigation: The incumbent approved-contract verifier recomputes Design evidence and validates the existing signed approval/engine receipt with a closed field set; pickup cannot author producer, result, or approval fields.

risks.risk: Stateless pickup writes hidden coordination state under another name.
risks.mitigation: pickup.py imports no loop/run/track/claim/lease/wave owner; tests instrument storage mutation entry points and compare an empty isolated home before/after start and second-checkout resume.

risks.risk: A parallel checkpoint or merge implementation drifts from BUILD-C.
risks.mitigation: Pickup calls explicit-input BUILD-C façades that reuse shared checkpoint and integration validation; repository.py remains the sole Git worktree/merge owner; severing pickup→BUILD-C fails AC3.

risks.risk: Receipt persistence creates an impossible self-referential Git commit SHA.
risks.mitigation: Receipt keys use the original authorized source SHA plus Design fingerprint and bind integrated tree/receipt digests, never the future evidence commit's SHA.

risks.risk: Resume accepts a fork, collision, or unrelated repository history.
risks.mitigation: Require one contiguous ordinal/predecessor chain and exact merged tree lineage for one source-SHA/fingerprint/element tuple; reject forks, gaps, overwrites, foreign receipts, and unexplained history before assignment.

risks.risk: Version metadata or release authority advances before functional proof.
risks.mitigation: Make 2.17.20 metadata the last functional checkpoint; bind quick security/QA and EM to one final clean SHA, then stop before push/tag/publication.

failure_modes.mode: Checkout or approved Design authority is dirty, stale, symlinked, outside the repository, or identity-mismatched.
failure_modes.recovery: The operator restores a clean exact authorized checkout and valid repository authority, then re-invokes pickup; no execution or receipt write occurs before that boundary.

failure_modes.mode: The signed approval or engine receipt is missing, forged, caller-authored, or bound to another SHA/fingerprint.
failure_modes.recovery: The Design authority owner supplies valid existing signed evidence for the exact repository bytes; pickup never repairs, re-signs, or downgrades the check.

failure_modes.mode: The current acceptance checkpoint is red, canceled, errored, stale, truncated, or mixed.
failure_modes.recovery: The assigned worker leaves the failed evidence intact, corrects only the same AC under manual authority, and reruns that checkpoint; later ACs and integration remain blocked.

failure_modes.mode: BUILD-C or the repository rejects exact revision, scope, predecessor, or merge identity.
failure_modes.recovery: The operator preserves the isolated worktree and receipt evidence, fixes the named identity mismatch, and retries the same AC; no alternate merge path is allowed.

failure_modes.mode: Receipt lineage has a collision, overwrite attempt, fork, gap, digest/path mismatch, or incompatible consumed outcome.
failure_modes.recovery: The operator restores the unique Git-tracked lineage or obtains a human scope decision; pickup writes no replacement over existing evidence and executes nothing while ambiguous.

failure_modes.mode: Pickup creates or resume reads private orchestration handoff state.
failure_modes.recovery: QA blocks the candidate; implementation removes the offending state edge and repeats AC1/AC4 from an empty home before any release metadata or review.

failure_modes.mode: Cold start reaches the first executing checkpoint at or after 120.0 seconds.
failure_modes.recovery: The pickup owner removes pre-checkpoint work such as scans/private bootstrap and reruns the fresh-process test; release remains blocked until the measured value is < 120.0 seconds.

observability.alerts_none_rationale: Pickup is a synchronous local CLI with no always-on service. Every refusal is immediate, named, and nonzero; durable signals live in the Git receipt/trace evidence, and the final quick security/QA plus EM reviews inspect them on one exact SHA.

rollout.strategy: After human Design and Plan authorization, deliver AC1 through AC5 as ordered manual checkpoints, one AC at a time with behavior and focused test in the same implementation commit. Keep loop/hooks unchanged. Update README, CHANGELOG, and all three manifests to 2.17.20 only after the functional path is green. Run security and QA quick passes concurrently on one final clean SHA, then EM on that SHA, and stop for explicit push authority.
rollout.rollback: There is no migration or replacement contract. Before sharing, abandon the isolated branch or normally revert the additive pickup commits. After sharing, use a forward revert that removes the pickup CLI/module/façades and restores prior version metadata while retaining committed export evidence. Never reset, force-push, delete receipts, move tags, mutate origin/main, or alter legacy loop/hook state.

visualization.reason: The initial exact-SHA authority path, one-AC BUILD-C sequence, post-merge receipt persistence, and private-store-free second-checkout resume are materially clearer as one boundary diagram.

lens_evidence.evidence: Grounded the adapter in tp.py, build_c.py, checkpoint.py, design_contract.py, repository.py, and storage.py; compared four materially distinct approaches; traced every AC to a named graph element and failing executable validation; checked numeric cold-start/zero-state targets, signal-linked failure recovery, additive rollback, and scope proportionality with no new signer, loop, checkpoint engine, merge engine, or private store.
